points.title: Unnormalised club register
points.must: The starting table PupilID, PupilName, Class, ClassTeacher, Clubs (list), and why it is not in 1NF.

points.title: Club register in 1NF
points.must: One row per pupil–club pair with composite key (PupilID, Club).

points.title: Club register in 2NF
points.must: Pupil fields depend only on PupilID → Pupils table; Memberships(PupilID*, Club).

points.title: Club register in 3NF
points.must: ClassTeacher depends on Class → Classes(Class, ClassTeacher); final design Classes, Pupils, Clubs, Memberships with keys marked.

points.title: Link (junction) table
points.must: Resolves a many-to-many relationship; its primary key is the composite of the two foreign keys, e.g. Memberships(PupilID*, ClubID*).

points.title: Relationships diagram
points.must: Classes 1:M Pupils, Pupils 1:M Memberships, Clubs 1:M Memberships.

points.title: A second scenario
points.must: Another full normalisation (e.g. clinic visits) through 1NF, 2NF and 3NF.

points.title: Steps to create the database
points.must: Create tables with data types, set primary keys, create foreign keys, create the “one” tables first, enter test data, test with join queries.

points.title: Referential integrity
points.must: Every foreign key value must match an existing primary key value; an insert with a non-existent class is rejected.

points.title: CREATE TABLE with keys
points.must: SQL with PRIMARY KEY, REFERENCES Table(Field), NOT NULL, and a composite PRIMARY KEY (a, b).

points.title: Join query
points.must: SELECT … FROM Pupils JOIN Classes ON Pupils.Class = Classes.Class (and more joins).

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: FK type differs from PK, tables created in the wrong order, two PRIMARY KEY words for a composite key.
